meta.triageRationale: One story with a clear approach and a small surface: activation already probes reachability and the plugin already has a lifecycle controller that starts the daemon through daemon-ctl.sh; start it once when the probe finds it stopped. Design points: consent/onboarding state, which probe states trigger a start, once per activation, failure reporting.

summary.prose: When VS Code starts and the extension finds an installed daemon that is not running, it now starts the daemon itself, once, and shows the result in the status bar. The start is a plain spawn of the daemon that is already built: it does not pull, install or build, so it never updates the daemon (updates stay behind the Update prompt of the freshness check). It starts only when the daemon is installed and reported stopped, never when it is merely erroring and never when it is not installed (installing stays the consented first-run step), and it checks once more just before starting that another window has not already started it. A start that fails, or that reports success but leaves the daemon unreachable, shows as an error with the reason and is not retried. The settings pull from the daemon, the daemon update check and the first-run onboarding, which all need a reachable daemon, now run once the probe and any start have settled, so they find the daemon up instead of failing while it is still stopped. A running daemon is left alone, and activation never blocks or throws.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Start the daemon when the extension activates and finds it stopped

api.name: ActivationDeps
api.signature: interface ActivationDeps { client: IpcClient; status: StatusSurface; probeTimeoutMs?: number | undefined; controller?: Pick<DaemonLifecycleController, 'isInstalled' | 'run'> | undefined; onSettled?: (() => void) | undefined }

parameters.name: controller
parameters.purpose: the daemon lifecycle controller, so activation can start an installed daemon that the probe finds stopped; absent means activation behaves exactly as today

parameters.name: onSettled
parameters.purpose: called once when the probe and any automatic start have finished, whatever their outcome, so work that needs a reachable daemon can follow them; absent means nothing is called

returns.meaning: the dependencies of the activation shell, with one optional addition

preconditions: the controller, when given, is the one extension.ts builds for the daemon commands
postconditions: a deps object without controller is valid and never starts anything
onSettled is called at most once per activation, never throws into activation, and is called also when the probe or the start failed

api.name: runReachabilityProbe
api.signature: function runReachabilityProbe(deps: ActivationDeps): Promise<DaemonUiState>  // was Promise<void>

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: the client to probe and the status surface to update

returns.meaning: the state the probe pushed into the status surface ('running', 'stopped' or 'errored'), so the caller can act on it; the status surface is updated exactly as before

errors.condition: a throwing or timed-out probe resolves 'errored', as today; it never rejects

postconditions: the status surface holds the returned state

api.name: startDaemonIfStopped
api.signature: function startDaemonIfStopped(deps: ActivationDeps, probed: DaemonUiState): Promise<void>  // new

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: the controller to start through and the status surface to update

returns.meaning: resolves once the start attempt, if any, is over; the status surface then shows the daemon running, or errored with the reason

errors.condition: a start that fails, throws, or reports success while the daemon is still not reachable leaves an errored status with the reason (the controller's message, or 'the daemon did not answer after start'); it never rejects

postconditions: a start is attempted only when probed is 'stopped', the controller reports the daemon installed, and a fresh reachability check made just before the start does not find it running
when that fresh check finds the daemon running, no start is made and the status shows running
the start is a plain start: it passes the controller's plain option, so nothing is pulled, installed or built
no start is attempted for 'running', 'errored' or 'unknown', or for a daemon that is not installed
at most one start is attempted per call, and the activation calls it once

api.name: DaemonLifecycleController.run
api.signature: run(action: LifecycleAction, options?: { plain?: boolean } | undefined): Promise<LifecycleResult>  // options is new

parameters.name: action
parameters.purpose: start, stop, restart or update, as today

parameters.name: options
parameters.purpose: plain: true adds --skip-sync, --skip-install and --skip-build to the daemon-ctl.sh command line, so a start only spawns the built daemon; absent or false runs the command exactly as today

returns.meaning: as today: ok and the true post-action reachability, with the reason on failure

errors.condition: a missing ctl script answers an errored result 'insrc daemon is not installed'; a non-zero exit answers an errored result with daemon-ctl.sh's reason (exit 4, 'the daemon git / npm / build / start step failed', is also what a start that did not become ready within 60 s gives); it never throws

postconditions: without options the command line is byte for byte what it is today, so the insrc.daemon.* commands and every other caller are unchanged

api.name: activateExtension

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: as before, plus the optional controller

returns.meaning: returns at once; the probe and then the start run in the background, and onSettled, when given, is called once they have finished

errors.condition: any failure in the probe or the start leaves the status 'errored' and is never thrown into activation

postconditions: activation does not wait for the probe or the start
the start, when it happens, comes after the probe has set 'stopped'

onSettled, when given, is called exactly once after the probe and any start have finished (the chain ends in a finally), also when either failed or threw; the call is wrapped so a throwing onSettled is contained

dataModelChanges.details: ActivationDeps gains the optional controller field. extension.ts passes the controller it already builds for the daemon commands. runReachabilityProbe returns the state it set instead of nothing, which its existing callers (activateExtension and the tests) can ignore. startDaemonIfStopped is new and lives in activation.ts beside the probe; activateExtension chains it after the probe in the same fire-and-forget background. Before it starts, it asks the client for reachability once more and does nothing if the daemon is now running (another window won the race). DaemonLifecycleController.run gains an optional options argument whose plain flag adds --skip-sync --skip-install --skip-build to the daemon-ctl.sh start, so the automatic start only spawns the already built daemon and never pulls, installs or builds; the daemon is updated only through the freshness check's Update prompt or the Update command. A start that returns ok with the daemon still not running is shown as errored with the detail 'the daemon did not answer after start'. No new setting, command, manifest entry or daemon change is made, and onboarding is untouched: it still offers installation behind consent. ActivationDeps also gains the optional onSettled callback, which activateExtension calls once after the probe and any start have finished. extension.ts uses it so that three things that need a reachable daemon wait for it: the settings pull from the daemon (configSync.pullFromDaemon), the daemon update check (runDaemonFreshnessCheck) and the first-run onboarding (runOnboarding). All three are unchanged in themselves; they now run after activation has settled instead of at once, so after an automatic start they find the daemon up (no 'could not read daemon config' toast, the settings mirror is synced, the Update prompt or the update check's plugin-upgrade update can happen in the same activation, and onboarding sees the true registration state), and when the daemon is not installed or the start fails they behave as before. The extension entry keeps the call shapes its source-scan tests pin: the onboarding IIFE keeps its guarded form and only begins with an await of the settled signal, the settings pull is still a .pullFromDaemon() call, and the update check call is wrapped so that it runs after the signal, with its wiring test's block pattern updated to accept the wrapped form. The settings sync engine, the update check module, onboarding and the registrar are not changed.

errorCases.scenario: The start fails (daemon-ctl.sh exits non-zero, for example because the daemon did not become ready within 60 seconds or a stale daemon could not be stopped)
errorCases.detection: controller.run('start', { plain: true }) answers ok:false with a message (its mapping of daemon-ctl.sh's exit codes, exit 4 for a start that did not become ready)
errorCases.response: The status surface shows errored with that message; the start is not retried in this activation
errorCases.userImpact: The status bar shows the daemon errored with why; the user can fix it and use the Start daemon command

errorCases.scenario: The start reports success but the daemon is still not reachable (slow to bind its socket, or it exited at once)
errorCases.detection: controller.run answers ok:true with a post-start state other than 'running'
errorCases.response: startDaemonIfStopped treats it as a failed start: the status surface shows errored with the detail 'the daemon did not answer after start'; it is not retried
errorCases.userImpact: The status bar shows errored with a reason, never a bare 'stopped'; the user can use the Start daemon command

errorCases.scenario: The controller throws instead of answering
errorCases.detection: the call to controller.isInstalled() or controller.run('start', { plain: true }) rejects inside startDaemonIfStopped
errorCases.response: It is caught; the status surface shows 'errored'; nothing is thrown into activation
errorCases.userImpact: The status bar shows errored; the daemon commands still work

errorCases.scenario: The probe cannot tell (it times out or throws)
errorCases.detection: runReachabilityProbe resolves 'errored' after the deadline or on an exception
errorCases.response: No start is attempted, since 'errored' may mean a daemon that is up but not answering; the status shows errored as today
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees errored and can restart the daemon by hand

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is stopped and not installed
errorCases.response: No start is attempted and the status stays 'stopped'; installing remains the consented first-run onboarding step
errorCases.userImpact: The user is offered installation by onboarding as before

edgeCases.input: the daemon is already running when VS Code starts
edgeCases.expected: The probe says 'running'; nothing is started

edgeCases.input: no controller is passed in the deps
edgeCases.expected: Activation behaves exactly as today: probe and status only

edgeCases.input: several VS Code windows start at once with the daemon stopped
edgeCases.expected: Each re-checks reachability just before starting and skips the start when another window has already brought the daemon up. Two windows that both pass the check in the same instant can still both start; daemon-ctl.sh start stops a daemon whose pid file is alive before it spawns, so they can restart each other's daemon before one remains. This narrow window is accepted, with no lock

edgeCases.input: the origin has newer commits than the installed daemon when the automatic start runs
edgeCases.expected: The daemon that is already built is started as it is; nothing is pulled. The update check runs after activation has settled, so it finds the daemon up and can offer the Update prompt in this same activation

edgeCases.input: the first-run onboarding and the update check, which also need the daemon
edgeCases.expected: Both run after activation has settled, so neither overlaps the start: onboarding's register offer reads the true registration state from a running daemon, and the update check finds the daemon up. When the daemon is not installed, onboarding's install offer comes after the probe, a few seconds later than before

edgeCases.input: the daemon is stopped and not installed, or the automatic start fails
edgeCases.expected: Activation still settles, then the settings pull, the update check and onboarding run and behave exactly as they do today with an unreachable daemon: the pull shows its 'could not read daemon config' toast, the update check skips silently, onboarding offers install

edgeCases.input: the daemon is already running at activation
edgeCases.expected: Activation settles after the probe, and the settings pull and the update check run then, one probe later than before; nothing else differs

edgeCases.input: the installed checkout was never built (no out/daemon/index.js)
edgeCases.expected: isInstalled() is false, so no start is attempted and the status stays 'stopped', as for a daemon that is not installed

edgeCases.input: the plugin was upgraded since the last activation, the daemon was stopped, and the automatic start brought it up
edgeCases.expected: The update check's own plugin-upgrade path (versionState current differs from last seen) then updates and restarts the daemon without a prompt, as it does today whenever the daemon is reachable at that point. This is accepted: before, a stopped daemon made the check skip and mark the new version as seen without updating

invariantsToPreserve.text: Activation never blocks and never throws: the probe and any start run in the background, and every failure ends as a status state
Installing the daemon stays behind the consent gate and the first-run onboarding; the extension starts only a daemon that is already installed
The lifecycle commands (insrc.daemon.start and the others) and their status reflection behave exactly as before: the controller's run without the new option builds the same command line
The automatic start itself never updates the daemon: updates come from the update check (its Update prompt, or its own plugin-upgrade path) and the Update command
A deps object without a controller leaves the activation's probe-only behaviour byte for byte as it is
The settings pull, the update check and onboarding keep their own behaviour, errors and notifications; only the moment they start changes, to after activation has settled

migration.stateBefore: On activation the extension fires a reachability probe and shows the result in the status surface; it never starts anything. ActivationDeps holds only the client, the status surface and an optional probe timeout, and an installed but stopped daemon stays stopped until the user runs the Start daemon command (activation.ts, daemon/commands.ts and extension.ts from the s1 bundles).
migration.stateAfter: The probe also reports the state it found. When that state is 'stopped' and the lifecycle controller says the daemon is installed, activation checks reachability once more and, if the daemon is still not up, starts it once as a plain start (no pull, install or build) and shows running, or errored with the reason. Everything else is as before. Activation then signals that it has settled, and the settings pull, the daemon update check and the first-run onboarding run after that signal instead of at once.

migrationSteps.action: Give the lifecycle controller's run an optional plain option that adds --skip-sync, --skip-install and --skip-build to the start command; without it the command line is unchanged
Make the reachability probe answer the state it pushed into the status surface, and add the optional controller to the activation's dependencies; with no controller given, behaviour is unchanged

Add the start-if-stopped step beside the probe (re-check reachability, plain start, success without reachability treated as failure) and chain it after the probe in the activation's background run, guarded to the stopped-and-installed case and to one attempt

Add the optional onSettled callback to the activation's dependencies, called once after the probe and any start have finished; in the extension entry, have the settings pull, the daemon update check and the first-run onboarding wait for it
Pass the daemon lifecycle controller from the extension entry into the activation, which is what turns the behaviour on

migration.backwardCompat: Additive and internal: the new activation dependency and the controller's new option are both optional, the probe's extra return value is ignored by its existing callers, and no command, setting, manifest entry, IPC or daemon behaviour changes. Removing the controller from the entry's call turns the feature off again.

alternativesConsidered.name: Start it inside the activation probe, silently, once
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: When the activation probe finds the daemon stopped and installed, run the controller's start once and show the result in the status surface.
alternativesConsidered.approach: ActivationDeps gains an optional controller. After the probe sets 'stopped', activation asks the controller whether the daemon is installed and, if so, runs start once and reflects its result (running, or errored with the controller's message) in the status surface, in the same fire-and-forget background as the probe. It starts only on 'stopped' (never on 'errored', where something is up but wrong), at most once per activation, and never when the daemon is not installed, since installing stays the consented onboarding step. A start that fails shows as errored with the reason and is not retried. Without a controller in the deps, activation behaves exactly as today. The start is a plain spawn (no pull, install or build) and a fresh reachability check just before it skips the start when another window already brought the daemon up.
pros: Smallest change: one dependency added to the existing probe, reusing the controller and the status surface
Matches the request: the daemon is up after a restart with no click
Starting an installed daemon is the same action as the insrc.daemon.start command, which already needs no consent
cons: Starts a background process without asking each time
No way to turn it off short of stopping the extension

alternativesConsidered.name: Start it silently, with a setting to turn it off
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same as a1, gated by a new insrc.daemon.autoStart setting that defaults to on.
alternativesConsidered.approach: As a1, but activation first reads a machine-scoped boolean setting insrc.daemon.autoStart (default true) and starts the daemon only when it is on. The setting is declared in the extension manifest and in the daemon's config catalog so the settings sync and the catalog-versus-manifest test stay in step.
pros: A user who does not want a background process started for them can turn it off
Same start behaviour as a1 when on
cons: A new setting touches the manifest, the daemon's config catalog and their parity tests, which is more than the request asked for
A second place to look when the daemon does not come up
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same behaviour with an opt-out, at the cost of the manifest and catalog changes the request did not ask for; it can be added later if wanted.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ask first with a Start button
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: When the probe finds the daemon stopped, show a notification with a Start button instead of starting it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: After the probe sets 'stopped' and the daemon is installed, activation shows a notification through the consent gate with a Start action; only an accept runs the controller's start. A decline or dismiss leaves the daemon stopped, and nothing is remembered.
pros: Nothing starts without the user saying so
cons: The user has to click on every VS Code start, which is the step they asked to be rid of
Does not meet the stated expectation that the daemon is started
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Does not start the daemon by itself, so it does not meet the request.

openQuestions: There is no setting to turn the automatic start off (alternative a2); it can be added later if wanted.
Two windows that pass the re-check in the same instant can still both start the daemon and restart each other's before one remains; this is accepted with no lock.
The Story has no acceptance criteria; ac1-ac5 were derived from its stated need and from the live check, where the settings pull raced the start.
